blocks.text: Le-Chatelier’s principle can be stated as follows:

blocks.title: Le-Chatelier’s principle
blocks.text: “If a system in equilibrium is disturbed, it behaves in such a way as to nullify the effect of that disturbance”.
Le-Chatelier’s principle describes what happens to a system when something momentarily takes it away from equilibrium.

blocks.alt: Box with the name Henry-Louis Le Chatelier at the top and the dates (1850-1936) below. Head-and-shoulders portrait turned slightly to the left: short grey hair brushed up, round wire-rimmed spectacles with a cord, a full moustache, a high white collar, a dark tie and a dark jacket, on a soft cream background.
blocks.caption: Henry-Louis Le Chatelier (1850-1936). A French chemist of the late 19th and early 20th centuries. He proposed the Le-Chatlier Principle, a significant achievement in chemistry (original drawing after the photograph printed in the textbook).
